To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) No black-box (k+1,?)robust combiner of collision-resistant hash-functions whose output is significantly smaller than what can be obtained by concatenating the outputs of any k+1 of the components can be built.

1. There exist no (non-trivial) (k,?)-robust combiners for collision-resistant hash functions whose output is significantly longer than the output of the trivial (k,?) combiner (which concatenates the output of the components).
(1) no black-box combiner exists that is significantly better than the trivial combiner and (2) no black-box (1,1)-combiner exists at all.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question.
the construction and analysis of combiners for collision-resistant hash functions, and the following results are obtained.
the question of whether there are non-trivial combiners which are secure even if the components of the combiner are not secure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no non-trivial black-box (k,n)-robust combiners for collision-resistant hash-function, and this holds even for the case where n=k+1.
the trivial combiner is the only practical way to get a black-box robust combiner for collision-resistance.
the only practical black-box combiners for collision-resistant hash functions are those which are not robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trivial construction of concatenating outputs is essentially optimal.
we show that there is a tradeoff between the robustness (the number of components which must be collision-resistant) and the efficiency (the length of the output) of black-box robust combiners.
we show the existence of a black-box combiner for collisionresistant hash functions is equivalent to the existence of a one-way function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
if one wants to get a collision-resistant hash-function from collision-resistant hash-functions which are not collision-resistant on the same domain, then one has to use non-trivial constructions.
in order to get a practical black-box (k,...) robust combiner, one has to use the combiner in a white-box way, i.e. the combiner should be a part of the application.
